correctness.rationale: For every rectangle after an exact pentagon-symmetry orientation reduction, the four relevant support inequalities hold with fixed signs for \(0\leq\theta\leq\pi/10\). Positive weights eliminate the rectangle center and give \((p+qt)A+(s-rt)B\leq\sqrt5/2\), where \(t=\tan\theta\). AM–GM gives the claimed area bound. The explicit formula for the center and half-edge parameters meets all four constraints with equality; the fifth-facet slack is exactly \((5-\sqrt5)t(1-t/\tan(\pi/10))/[8(p+qt)(s-rt)]\), nonnegative on the full parameter interval. Thus every orientation upper bound is attained. Positive weights and strict AM–GM equality give a unique rectangle for each actual orientation, and a sine-endpoint comparison gives five global copies. Endpoint angles and circumradius scaling are covered. All critical identities were independently recomputed from radicals and the standalone `verify.py` was run at the actual package-source path. Random and finite-precision checks were not used to infer the universal theorem.

originality.rationale: The 2014 general exact convex-polygon rectangle algorithm guarantees a computational solution but neither an analytic pentagon area–orientation envelope nor complete equality cases. The 2017 question and responses anticipate the maximizing configuration and a normalized numerical value, explicitly relying on unproved symmetry/contact assumptions; those aspects are credited and not presented as new. The 2015 pentagon-cover theorem fixes perimeter and varies rectangle shape, reversing the containment quantifiers; it does not entail the fixed-pentagon area envelope. The indexed result for regular even polygons excludes the pentagon. The present orientation-wise exact formula, positive dual support certificate, unconditional attainment for all orientations, uniqueness and five global maximizers are additional mathematically non-implied statements across these inspected sources. Historical risk remains: no assertion of worldwide priority.
residual_risks: The 2017 mathematical discussion anticipates the extremal configuration and numerical value; independent priority attaches only to the unconditional proof and orientation-wise classification, not to this anticipated candidate.
Older book or forum arguments under other terminology could contain the same dual support certificate; external query coverage is not exhaustive.
The most similar 2026 even-polygon finding was only inspectable through its published index; it expressly excludes odd n and poses no decisive overlapping theorem.
The 2014 general algorithm may compute the value after specific implementation, so the present result is an explicit structural evaluation rather than a novelty claim for computability.

value.rationale: A natural precise invariant in classical geometric optimization: the orientation-dependent envelope of the largest rectangle contained in a fixed regular pentagon. A publicly posed 2017 problem contained only conditional symmetry/contact analyses, so replacing assumptions by a positive, globally valid support certificate is substantive, not a routine substitution. The all-orientation formula answers how optimum area changes under rotation; it also gives a complete five-element optimizer classification and the exact global extremum. The result is narrower than a general-odd-n theorem but an exact self-contained natural geometric extremum, with a reusable geometric dual method.
